subject.title: Bug: Poe image/video-output models are accepted in config but fail at runtime (Nano Banana 400, Veo/Sora fallback)

question: Should OpenClaw treat non-text-output provider models as unsupported in chat/session runtime with an explicit diagnostic, or should it add first-class image/video-output chat runtime support?
rationale: Current code has no output-modality contract, while either rejection or support changes public config, provider routing, fallback, and user-facing model-selection semantics.

options.title: Reject unsupported chat outputs
options.body: Add output-modality metadata/validation only as needed to fail clearly for image/video-output chat models while keeping generated media on `image_generate` and `video_generate`.

options.title: Build media-output chat runtime
options.body: Design broader image/video response handling across model selection, provider request construction, generated-media lifecycle, and channel rendering.

options.title: Document tool-only support
options.body: Clarify docs and model-list UX that media generation is tool-only, but accept that custom config may still need a sharper runtime error later.

recommendation.title: Reject unsupported chat outputs
recommendation.body: Add output-modality metadata/validation only as needed to fail clearly for image/video-output chat models while keeping generated media on `image_generate` and `video_generate`.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the separate image-generation tool path and is the best available owner for the product boundary between chat runtime and media-generation tools.
